data.title: Allied Critical Metals Files First Quarter Financial Statements and Appoints New Chief Financial Officer
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Allied Critical Metals Inc. (OTCQB: ACMIF) (FSE: 0VJ0) ("Allied" or the "Company") announced today the release of its unaudited consolidated financial statements for the first quarter of 2026, together with its Management Discussion and Analysis (the "Financial Disclosures"). The Financial Disclosures will be posted on the Company's website at www.alliedcritical.com and on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca. All values in the Financial Disclosures are in United States dollars unless otherwise stated.

The Company is also pleased to announce the appointment of John Chou as its new Chief Financial Officer. John Chou is a senior finance executive with more than 25 years of experience in financial management, corporate finance, accounting, taxation and public-company reporting. He has held senior finance leadership positions across the natural resources, energy and consumer sectors. Mr. Chou previously served as Vice-President of Finance at Gran Colombia Gold Corp. (now Aris Mining Corporation), where he was involved in the financial management of a publicly traded gold mining company with significant operations in Colombia. Prior to that, he served as Vice-President of Finance at Frontera Energy Corp., a publicly listed South American oil and gas company, where he gained extensive experience in the financial management of an international resource business. Earlier in his career, Mr. Chou held financial and accounting positions with Deloitte, where he developed a strong foundation in financial reporting, assurance and taxation. Mr. Chou is a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA, CA), holds an MBA from the Schulich School of Business at York University and a Bachelor of Commerce degree from the University of Toronto's Rotman School of Management.

Roy Bonnell, Chief Executive Officer of Allied Critical Metals, commented, "We are very pleased to welcome John to the Company as Chief Financial Officer. John brings a wealth of experience in public-company finance, with an impressive track record in the resource sector, including senior finance roles at Gran Colombia Gold and Frontera Energy. His experience managing financial operations, reporting and corporate finance at publicly traded resource companies will be invaluable as we advance our projects and execute on our growth strategy. We look forward to working with John as we enter this next phase of the Company's development."

The Company would also like to thank Sean Choi for his contributions and commitment during his tenure as Chief Financial Officer and wishes him every success in his future endeavours. Sean will assist with an orderly transition to ensure continuity in the Company's financial reporting and operations.

About Allied Critical Metals Inc.

Allied Critical Metals Inc. is a Canadian-based mining company focused on the advancement and revitalization of its 100%-owned Borralha Tungsten Project and the Vila Verde Tungsten Project in northern Portugal.

The Borralha Project is one of the largest undeveloped tungsten resources globally and benefits from a favourable Environmental Impact Declaration (DIA), positioning the Project for advancement toward feasibility and development. Vila Verde represents additional exploration upside within the same strategic jurisdiction. In October 2026, the Borralha Project was selected as a Strategic Project under the European Union's Critical Raw Materials Act, the only Portuguese project and the only tungsten extraction project included in the European Commission's latest selection.

Tungsten has been designated a critical raw material by the United States and the European Union due to its strategic importance in defense, aerospace, manufacturing, automotive, electronics and energy applications. Currently, China, Russia and North Korea account for approximately 87% of global tungsten supply and reserves, highlighting the importance of secure western sources.

Further details regarding the Borralha Project are available in the Company's current preliminary economic assessment technical report prepared in accordance with NI 43-101 entitled "NI 43-101 Technical Report Preliminary Economic Assessment, Borralha Tungsten Project, Parish of Salto, District of Vila Real, Portugal", dated effective April 14, 2026, which is published on the Company's website at www.alliedcritical.com and under its profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

data.title: Alerian MLP ETF Tax Update
data.description:
Alerian MLP ETF (the “Fund” or “AMLP”) has modified the estimate of the Fund’s deferred tax liability and recorded a tax accrual adjustment of approximately $(2.8) million (approximately $0.012 per share) into the net asset value (NAV) of the Fund on November 30, 2026. As part of the tax accrual adjustment, the Fund’s deferred tax liability (DTL) has decreased primarily due to updated tax reporting and other tax related modifications that are routine for the Fund's tax analysis. The Fund will rely to a large extent on information provided by the MLPs, which is largely reported on a delayed basis and is not necessarily timely, to estimate deferred tax liability for purposes of financial statement reporting and determining the NAV. From time to time, the Adviser will modify the estimates or assumptions regarding the Fund’s deferred tax liability as new information becomes available and may consider, among other matters, the duration of statutory carryforward periods, shareholder transactions, underlying index constituent changes and market conditions. The Fund’s estimates regarding its deferred tax liability are made in good faith; however, the daily estimate of the Fund’s deferred tax liability used to calculate the Fund’s NAV could vary significantly from the Fund’s actual tax liability.

ALPS Portfolio Solutions Distributor, Inc. is also the distributor for the Alerian Energy Infrastructure ETF and the ALPS | Alerian Energy Infrastructure Portfolio. Please direct any inquiries to info@alerianmlp.com or by calling 1-866-759-5679.

An investor should consider the investment objectives, risks, charges and expenses carefully before investing. To obtain a prospectus containing this and other information, call 1-866-759-5679 or visit www.alpsfunds.com. Read the prospectus carefully before investing.

Shares of ETFs are bought and sold at market price (not NAV) and are not individually redeemable.

All investments are subject to risks, including the loss of money and the possible loss of the entire principal amount invested. Additional information regarding the risks of this investment is available in the prospectus.

Investments in securities of Master Limited Partnerships (MLPs) involve risks that differ from an investment in common stock. MLPs are controlled by their general partners, which generally have conflicts of interest and limited fiduciary duties to the MLP, which may permit the general partner to favor its own interests over the MLPs.

A portion of the benefits you are expected to derive from the Fund’s investment in MLPs depends largely on the MLPs being treated as partnerships for federal income tax purposes. As a partnership, an MLP has no federal income tax liability at the entity level. Therefore, treatment of one or more MLPs as a corporation for federal income tax purposes could affect the Fund’s ability to meet its investment objective and would reduce the amount of cash available to pay or distribute to you. Legislative, judicial, or administrative changes and differing interpretations, possibly on a retroactive basis, could negatively impact the value of an investment in MLPs and therefore the value of your investment in the Fund.

The Fund invests primarily in a particular sector and could experience greater volatility than a fund investing in a broader range of industries.

Investments in the energy infrastructure sector are subject to: reduced volumes of natural gas or other energy commodities available for transporting, processing or storing; changes in the regulatory environment; extreme weather and; rising interest rates which could result in a higher cost of capital and drive investors into other investment opportunities.

All K-1s are received and processed by the Alerian MLP ETF. The Alerian MLP ETF distributes a single Form 1099 to its shareholders. This notice is provided to you for informational purposes only and should not be considered tax advice. Please consult your tax advisor for further assistance.

If, due to tax law changes or for other reasons, an MLP in the portfolio is deemed to be taxable as a corporation rather than a partnership for federal income purposes, then income would be subject to federal income taxation at the MLP level. This would reduce the amount of cash available for distribution to the fund which could result in a reduction of the fund’s value. The Fund is taxed as a regular corporation for federal income purposes, which reduces the net asset value of fund shares by the accrual of any deferred tax liabilities. Depending on the taxes paid by the fund as a result of income and/or gains from investments and/or the sale of MLP interests, the return on an investment in the Fund will be reduced. This differs from most investment companies, which elect to be treated as “regulated investment companies” to avoid paying entity level income taxes. The ETF is taxed as a regular corporation and is subject to US federal income tax on taxable income at the corporate tax rate (currently as high as 21%) as well as state and local taxes.

The Fund is classified for federal income tax purposes as a taxable regular corporation or so-called Subchapter “C” corporation. As a “C” corporation, the Fund accrues deferred tax liability for its future tax liability associated with the capital appreciation of its investments and the distributions received by the Fund on equity securities of master limited partnerships considered to be a return of capital and for any net operating gains. The Fund’s accrued deferred tax liability, if any, is reflected each day in the Fund’s net asset value per share. The deferred income tax expense/(benefit) represents an estimate of the Fund’s potential tax expense/(benefit) if it were to recognize the unrealized gains/(losses) in the portfolio. An estimate of deferred income tax expense/(benefit) is dependent upon the Fund’s net investment income/(loss) and realized and unrealized gains/(losses) on investments and such expenses may vary greatly from year to year and from day to day depending on the nature of the Fund’s investments, the performance of those investments and general market conditions. Therefore, any estimate of deferred income tax expense/(benefit) cannot be reliably predicted from year to year.

The Fund employs a “passive management” - or indexing - investment approach and seeks investment results that correspond (before fees and expenses) generally to the performance of its underlying index. Unlike many investment companies, the Fund is not “actively” managed. Therefore, it would not necessarily sell or buy a security unless that security is removed from or added to the underlying index, respectively.

data.title: UraniumX Announces Flow-Through Private Placement
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / UraniumX Discovery Corp. (the "Company" or "UraniumX") is pleased to announce a non-brokered private placement of up to 36,363,636 flow-through shares at a price of $0.055 per FT Share for aggregate gross proceeds of up to $2,000,000 (each a "FT Share") (the "Offering"). No warrants will be issued to subscribers in connection with the Offering. The Company may increase the size of the Offering to accommodate additional demand.

The FT Shares will qualify as "flow-through shares" within the meaning of subsection 66(15) of the Income Tax Act (Canada). The Company intends to use the gross proceeds from the sale of FT Shares to incur eligible" Canadian exploration expenses" that qualify as "flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures" within the meaning of subsection 127(9) of the Income Tax Act (Canada), which will be renounced to the subscribers in an amount not less than the subscription price of the FT Shares, with an effective date no later than December 31, 2026 and to incur such expenses on or before December 31, 2027.

Proceeds will fund the Company's ongoing exploration activities at Murphy Lake.

Closing of the Offering is subject to receipt of all necessary corporate and regulatory approvals, including the approval of the Canadian Securities Exchange. All securities issued under the Offering will be subject to a statutory hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance.

The Company may pay finder's fees to eligible persons in connection with the Offering, in accordance with the policies of the Canadian Securities Exchange.

About UraniumX Discovery Corp.

UraniumX Discovery Corp. is a Canadian-based junior uranium exploration company focused on advancing uranium properties in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin, one of Canada's most active uranium districts. The Company's flagship Murphy Lake Uranium Property is located in the northeastern Athabasca Basin, where UraniumX is earning up to a 70% interest through an option agreement with F4 Uranium Corp. UraniumX additionally holds 100% interests in the Zoo Bay and NeoCore uranium properties, and is advancing a project generator approach across its broader portfolio by optioning non-core assets while retaining royalties and equity, allowing the Company to concentrate exploration capital on Murphy Lake.

data.title: Integrated Quantum Technologies Announces Adoption of Semi-Annual Financial Reporting
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Integrated Quantum Technologies Inc. (OTCQB: IGCRF) (FSE: Y4G1) (the "Company" or "IQT"), an enterprise AI security and infrastructure technology company, announces that it intends to adopt semi-annual financial reporting pursuant to Coordinated Blanket Order 51-933 - Exemptions to Permit Semi-Annual Reporting for Certain Venture Issuers (the "Blanket Order").

The Blanket Order allows eligible venture issuers to voluntarily transition from quarterly to semi-annual financial reporting, reducing the administrative and financial burden associated with quarterly reporting while maintaining applicable continuous disclosure obligations.

Semi-Annual Reporting

Pursuant to the Blanket Order, the Company will not file interim financial statements or related management's discussion and analysis ("MD&A") for the three-month interim period ending September 30, 2026.

The Company will continue to file interim financial statements and related MD&A for its six-month interim period, as well as annual financial statements and related MD&A, in accordance with applicable securities legislation.

The Company will also continue to comply with its ongoing continuous disclosure obligations, including the timely disclosure of material changes and significant corporate developments.

This news release is being filed pursuant to CSA Coordinated Blanket Order 51-933 Exemptions to Permit Semi-Annual Reporting for Certain Venture Issuers.

data.title: Green Rise Foods Inc. Announces Final Consideration Payable to Shareholders Pursuant to Arrangement with Pereira Verde Inc. and Filing of Appraisals for Greenhouse Properties
data.description:
Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Green Rise Foods Inc. ("Green Rise" or the "Company") announces that, further to its news release dated October 19, 2026 announcing the definitive arrangement agreement (the "Arrangement Agreement") whereby Pereira Verde Inc. (the "Purchaser") will acquire all of the issued and outstanding common shares of the Company ("Shares") not held by Vincent Narang, George Hatzoglou and certain persons associated with them (collectively, the "Excluded Securityholders") by way of a statutory plan of arrangement under the Business Corporations Act (Ontario) (the "Transaction"), the cash consideration to be received by each shareholder of the Company (the "Shareholders"), other than the Excluded Securityholders, will be $0.43 for each Share held (subject to any applicable withholding) (the "Consideration").

In accordance with the terms of the Arrangement Agreement, the Consideration remained at $0.43 per Share based on the estimated working capital of the Company (as calculated in accordance with the Arrangement Agreement, which excludes certain indebtedness and closing costs) as of the effective date of the Transaction (the "Estimated Working Capital"), as compared to the target working capital of negative $3.1 million (the "Target Working Capital").

The annual and special meeting of Shareholders and holders of options to purchase Shares (collectively, "Securityholders") to approve the Transaction (the "Meeting") will be held on December 4, 2026, and it is anticipated that the Transaction will close on or about December 11, 2026. Following closing of the Transaction, the Shares will be delisted from the TSX Venture Exchange (the "TSXV"). Copies of the management information circular of the Company dated November 3, 2026 (the "Circular") and the Arrangement Agreement are available under the Company's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

Greenhouse Appraisals

The Company also announces that appraisals (the "Appraisals") previously prepared by an independent real estate appraisal firm in respect of each of the Company's three greenhouse farm properties (the "Properties") have been made available to Securityholders. The Appraisals were prepared in July 2026 in connection with negotiations with the Company's lenders and possible refinancing of the mortgages on the Properties. Securityholders can access the Appraisals under the Company's profile on SEDAR+ and may also request a copy of the Appraisals to be sent without charge by contacting Enrico (Rick) Paolone, Interim Chief Executive Officer and Board Chair of the Company, at rpaolone@greenrisefoods.ca or 416.669.1550.

The Appraisals appraised the Properties with the following market values as at the dates of such Appraisals (as defined in the Appraisals and subject to certain assumptions and conditions set out therein): (i) $52,997,000 estimated market value for the greenhouse property located at 2633 Albuna Townline, Town of Kingsville, ON ("GR1"), (ii) $19,843,000 estimated market value for the greenhouse property located at 1921 Road 3 East, Town of Kingsville, ON, and (iii) $17,700,000 estimated market value for the greenhouse property located at 795 Road 4 East, Town of Kingsville, ON. The Appraisals were prepared by an independent real estate appraisal firm in accordance with the Canadian Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice.

As disclosed in the Circular, the special committee of independent directors of the Company (the "Special Committee") compared the Appraisals to offers received for the individual Properties pursuant to the Company's strategic review process and determined that in order to derive any per-Share indication of value from the Appraisals, a series of significant adjustments and assumptions would have to be made, including:

  • the Appraisals do not reflect the value of the Properties as held and operated, especially in respect of GR1 which Appraisal does not account for the restrictive covenants that run with the property, the operating restrictions and shared infrastructure with Mastronardi Produce Limited, the Transaction ROFR (as defined in the Circular) nor potentially less replacement cost for new double poly greenhouse capacity;

  • the appraised values do not take into account the mortgages and other indebtedness secured on the Properties and the liquidity implication of such debt in light of negotiations with the Company's lenders;

  • any realization of the appraised values would require a sale of the Properties and would trigger recapture and capital gains tax on disposition; and

  • there would be further significant dividend "tax leakage" in distributing the net proceeds of the disposition of individual Properties to Shareholders.

In light of the foregoing and the offers received for the individual Properties, and considering the advice of Blair Franklin Capital Partners Inc., financial advisor to the Special Committee, as to the fairness, from a financial point of view, of the Consideration to be received by Shareholders (other than the Excluded Securityholders) pursuant to the Transaction, the Special Committee was of the view that the Appraisals should not reasonably affect the decision of Securityholders in evaluating the Transaction.

About the Company

Green Rise uses its wholly-owned 89 acres of Controlled-Environment Agriculture Greenhouses to produce high-quality fresh produce under the "SUNSET" brand for Mastronardi Produce Ltd, our distribution partner. Green Rise is proud to be an environmentally sustainable investment providing bee-pollinated, high-quality fresh products to meet the growing consumer demand for locally grown fresh produce.

More information about the Company is available at www.greenrisefoods.ca or under the Company's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Theralase® Technologies Inc.  (OTCQB: TLTFF) ("Theralase®" or the "Company"), a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company dedicated to the research and development of energy-activated small molecules for the safe and effective destruction of various cancers, bacteria and viruses, releases its unaudited condensed interim consolidated financial statements ("Financial Statements") for the nine-month period ended September 30th, 2026.

Theralase® will host a conference call on Wednesday, December 9th, 2026, at 11:00 am ET to discuss the Company's financial and operational results and provide an update on its clinical development programs. Financial Highlights:

For the nine-month period ended September 30th, 2026 compared to September 30th, 2025 (all funds in Canadian dollars):

  • Total revenue decreased 11% to $527,506 from $590,573. The TLC-2000 Cool Laser Therapy system represented 87% of sales, compared to 79%.

  • Canadian revenue decreased 8% to $507,492 from $550,453; US revenue decreased 47% to $20,014 from $37,741; international revenue decreased 100% to nil from $2,379.

  • Cost of sales decreased 20% to $238,703 from $299,743.

  • Gross margin was $288,803 (55% of revenue), compared to $290,830 (49%).

  • Selling expenses increased 3% to $218,163 from $212,421.

  • Administrative expenses increased 8% to $1,556,197 from $1,444,687 (primarily reflecting increases in investor relations, administrative salaries, amortization and depreciation allocation and general administrative expenses).

  • Net research and development expenses decreased 26% to $1,570,095 from $2,116,540 (primarily due to decreased costs associated with Study II patient enrollment and treatment).

  • Net loss decreased 12% to $3,013,858 (includes $499,263 of non-cash expenses) from $3,435,145 (includes $718,197 of non-cash expenses).

  • The Drug Division accounted for $2,496,298 (83%) of the net loss.

  • Cash used in operating activities increased 24% to $2,552,478 from $2,057,733.

For the nine-month period ended September 30th, 2026 compared to December 31st, 2025 (all funds in Canadian dollars):

  • Cash increased 3838% to $7,204,200 from $182,914.

  • Working capital increased 1860% to $7,907,730 from $403,506.

  • Shareholders' equity increased 416% to $9,181,261 from $1,777,816.

  • Outstanding short-term loans decreased to nil from $255,935.

Financing Highlights

During the nine-month period ended September 30th, 2026, Theralase® successfully completed a series of brokered and non-brokered private placements, generating approximately $9.7 million in net cash proceeds.

On August 24, 2026, the Company closed a brokered private placement pursuant to the Listed Issuer Financing Exemption, issuing 14,812,500 units at $0.24 per unit for aggregate gross proceeds of $3,555,000.

These financings have significantly strengthened the Company's financial position and provided additional resources to advance its lead bladder cancer clinical program, expand its oncology pipeline and support ongoing research and development activities.

The Company has raised approximately $17.9 million over the last two years through brokered and non-brokered private placements in support of its R&D programs. The Company is working with a full-service investment bank in Canada for future financings and has identified a full-service investment bank in the United States to advise on potential financings and US listing opportunities. Additional financing remains necessary to support ongoing operations and development activities.

Operational Highlights

Phase II NMIBC Clinical Study - Cohort 1

Study II (NCT03945162) is a Phase II, open-label, single-arm, multi-center study conducted in Canada and the United States, evaluating Ruvidar® activated by the TLC-3200 Medical Laser System ("Study Procedure") in patients with BCG-Unresponsive Non-Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer ("NMIBC") Carcinoma In-Situ ("CIS") (with or without resected papillary disease) ("Study II").

Theralase® has completed enrollment in Study II, with the CSSs enrolling and providing the primary Study Procedure to 97 patients, exceeding the 90 patients calculated in the statistical analysis plan.

Note: In the following clinical analysis, 2 patients who were considered BCG-Intolerant were removed to analyze only BCG-Unresponsive patients, leaving 95 patients in Study II.

According to the clinical study design, a patient is considered to have completed Study II, if they received the Study Procedure and have been assessed by the Principal Investigator ("PI") for up to 15 months or they have been prematurely removed from the clinical study by the PI for failure to respond or failure to comply with the clinical study design.

According to this definition, for BCG-Unresponsive patients 85 have completed Study II and 10 patients remain on study pending clinical data.

The following interim clinical data support the Study II endpoints:

Of the 95 patients enrolled and treated, 81% were ≥ 65 years of age, 82% male and 83% white. Tumor stage was distributed as follows: 82% pure CIS; 12% CIS + T1; and 6% CIS + Ta. 100% were classified as BCG-Unresponsive. The median number of BCG instillations was 12.

As of November 27th, 2026, 91 patients have been assessed for the primary endpoint, 55 for the secondary endpoint and 85 for the tertiary endpoint.

Primary Endpoint Performance (Complete Response at any Point in Time)

The primary endpoint of Study II is the achievement of CR at any point in time following the Study Procedure. Interim analysis demonstrates that 60.4% (55/91) evaluable patients achieved CR. A Total Response ("TR") was achieved by 69.2% (63/91) of evaluable patients.

Note: Total Response ("TR") includes CR and Indeterminate Response ("IR"), defined as negative cystoscopy (no evidence of Urothelial Cell Carcinoma ("UCC") in the bladder) and positive / suspicious urine cytology (detection of cancer in the urine, without a negative confirmatory bladder biopsy, suggesting UCC in the renal system other than the bladder).

Secondary Endpoint Performance (Duration of CR - 12 Months)

The secondary endpoint evaluates the sustainability of CR at 12 months, after initial CR determination (450 days post-treatment). Among patients evaluable for durability of response, 40.8% (20/49) patients maintained a CR at 450 days. A TR was achieved by 44.9% (22/49) of evaluable patients. Biopsy-confirmed CR: 95%. Median follow-up: 330 days.

The current median duration of response is 9 months (95% CI: 7.2, 10.6).

The predicted median duration of response, according to Kaplan-Meier's analysis, is 12 months.

Tertiary Endpoint Performance (Safety)

The tertiary endpoint is defined as patients who have a Serious Adverse Event ("SAE") ≥ 4 directly caused by the Study Drug or Study Device, which did not resolve within 450 days.

Theralase® and the independent Data Safety Monitoring Board believe all SAEs reported to date are unrelated or unlikely related to the Study Drug or Study Device.

Note: A SAE is defined as any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose: Is serious or life-threatening, requires inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization, results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity, is a congenital anomaly/birth defect or results in death.

Treatment Emergent Adverse Events ("TEAEs") were noted, but did not meet the SAE criteria. TEAEs included hematuria (73%), urinary frequency (67%) and urinary urgency (63%), which had a median resolution of 15, 36 and 43 days, respectively.

Cystectomy-free rate was 89% at 1 year and 80% at 3 years.

For Adverse Events ("AEs") reported there were: 65% Grade I, 33% Grade II, 1% Grade III and 1% Grade IV. All Grade I to Grade IV SAEs were resolved between 1 to 82 days. There were three Grade V SAEs that were considered unrelated or unlikely related to the Study Drug, Study Device or Study Procedure. Of the 25 SAEs, 92% were not TEAEs.

Duration of CR - Extended Time Points

Patients who have completed Study II were followed for up to 3 years after initial treatment at extended time points.

One patient demonstrated CR for 7 years, after one Study Procedure.

On Kaplan-Meier analysis, if CR is obtained, the long term estimated probability of remaining cancer free at 1, 2 and 3 years is 52.3%, 38.2% and 27.5%, respectively.

The interim clinical results support light-activated Ruvidar® as a potential bladder-preserving treatment option for patients diagnosed with BCG-Unresponsive NMIBC CIS, with or without papillary disease.

Regulatory Pathway, Commercialization Strategy and FDA Guidance

If approved by Health Canada and the FDA, the clinical data collected from Study II represents a transformative therapeutic option for patients diagnosed with BCG-Unresponsive NMIBC CIS, who would otherwise face radical cystectomy (surgical removal of the bladder).

The Theralase® Study Procedure has demonstrated a robust CR and sustained durability of that response, with the majority of patients receiving only a single Study Procedure (51%).

Theralase® is currently analyzing and compiling the clinical data for a New Drug Submission to Health Canada and a New Drug Application to the United States Food and Drug Administration with marketing decisions anticipated in 2027.

In 2027, Theralase® will pursue licensing agreements of the bladder cancer technology for global marketing and distribution of light-activated Ruvidar®.

Cohort 2

Theralase®, in conjunction with Ferring Pharmaceutical, is enrolling patients into a combinational clinical study to investigate the safety and efficacy of combining light-activated Ruvidar® with Adstiladrin.

It is anticipated that the complementary mechanisms of action (Ruvidar® targets bladder cancer cells directly, Adstiladrin® targets health bladder cells to produce Interferon to stimulate the innate and adaptive immune system) will provide a strong additive effect in the treatment of patients being treated for BCG-Unresponsive NMIBC CIS.

In the Study Procedure, patients will be treated with Ruvidar® (1 hour of drug instillation, 1 hour of light activation), then at another visit, they will be instilled with Adstiladrin® (1 hour procedure), both in outpatient procedures. Under the clinical protocol, the patient may receive up to 4 treatments of Adstiladrin® in total.

The presiding uro-oncologist will have the option to deliver an additional re-induction Study Procedure, if the patient recurs.

The patient will be followed for 15 months after initial Study Procedure and up to 3 years for post-study follow-up.

Commercialization and Strategic Partnerships

In parallel with the finalization of Study II, Theralase® is pursuing commercialization opportunities and strategic partnerships to support the global marketing and distribution of Ruvidar®. The Company is interested in engaging in discussions with pharmaceutical companies regarding:

  • Licensing arrangements for Ruvidar® in the treatment of BCG-Unresponsive NMIBC CIS in various geographic territories
  • Collaborative clinical research initiatives focused on the application of light-activated Ruvidar® for broader NMIBC indications
  • Collaborative clinical research combining Ruvidar®, with other FDA-approved drugs to enhance treatment efficacy

Product Stability and Logistics

Ruvidar® has demonstrated a shelf life of >10 years at room temperature, which supports both the long-term stability of the molecule and the practical logistics of clinical storage and distribution. This extended shelf life is expected to be a key differentiator in clinical and commercial settings, enabling medical facilities to store and deploy Ruvidar®, as needed, without significant cold chain and degradation concerns.

Expansion of the Oncology Pipeline - Rutherrin®

On September 15th, 2026, the Company commenced Good Laboratory Practice ("GLP") toxicology analysis of intravenously administered Rutherrin®. The program is designed to determine the Maximum Tolerated Dose and Human Equivalent Dose to provide starting and therapeutic doses for future human clinical studies. Completion is expected by the end of 2026, with results anticipated in early 2027.

Subject to receipt of toxicology reports and regulatory approval, the Company plans to advance Phase 0/I/II adaptive clinical development for glioblastoma multiforme, non-small cell lung cancer and muscle-invasive bladder cancer, followed by pancreatic cancer and colorectal cancer.

Phase 0 will evaluate tumour localization; Phase I/II will evaluate safety, dosing and therapeutic efficacy following multiple doses with radiation activation. Preclinical findings support further investigation, but do not establish human safety or efficacy.

Herpes Simplex Virus Type 1 ("HSV-1")

Theralase® continues preclinical development of topical Ruvidar® for HSV-1 lesions. Laboratory research demonstrated inhibition of HSV-1 replication at lower concentrations than acyclovir and additive / synergistic effects in combination experiments. Preclinical mouse model research supports further investigation of topical Ruvidar®. Human safety and efficacy remain to be established.

Roger DuMoulin-White, President and Chief Executive Officer of Theralase®, stated: "Throughout 2026, Theralase® has focused on strengthening its financial position, advancing its lead bladder cancer clinical program and expanding its therapeutic development pipeline. With patient enrollment completed in Study II, our priority in 2027 is the analysis and compilation of the clinical data of Study II required for regulatory submissions and successful marketing approval by Health Canada and the FDA, representing an important next step toward the potential commercialization of light-activated Ruvidar®. In parallel, our collaborative clinical development agreement with Ferring Pharmaceuticals and the completion of GLP toxicology for intravenously administered Rutherrin® provide opportunities to expand the clinical application of our energy-activated small molecule technology for numerous oncological conditions. With approximately $7.2 million in cash and $7.9 million in working capital as of September 30th, 2026, Theralase® is focused on advancing these important clinical and regulatory milestones, while maintaining financial discipline and building long-term shareholder value."

About Study II

Study II utilizes the therapeutic dose of the patented drug, Ruvidar® (TLD-1433), activated by the TLC-3200 Medical Laser System. Study II has enrolled and treated 95 BCG-Unresponsive NMIBC CIS (with or without resected Ta/T1) patients across 11 clinical study sites located in Canada and the United States.

About Adstiladrin

Adstiladrin® (nadofaragene firadenovec-vncg) is an FDA-approved intravesical non-replicating gene therapy for the treatment of adult patients with high-risk BCG-unresponsive NMIBC CIS with or without papillary tumors (±Ta/T1). It is a non-replicating adenovirus vector-based therapy containing the gene interferon alfa-2b, administered locally as a monotherapy by catheter directly into the bladder once every three months. The vector enters the cells of the bladder wall, releasing the active gene and causing the bladder's cell walls to secrete high and transient local expression of interferon alfa-2b protein, a naturally occurring protein the body uses to fight cancer. This approach essentially turns the bladder wall cells into interferon micro factories, enhancing the body's own natural defenses against the cancer.
